title: BatchSampler: Sampling Mini-Batches for Contrastive Learning in Vision, Language, and Graphs

problem.claim: Contrastive learning relies on effective negative sharing and hard-negative sampling within mini-batches.

gap.claim: Hard-negative quality is bounded by the current mini-batch, and false negatives remain an issue.

contributions.claim: BatchSampler samples mini-batches from the input data for contrastive learning.
The method designs a proximity graph of randomly selected instances to reduce false negatives within each mini-batch.
Random walk with restart on the proximity graph samples hard-to-distinguish instances, and the technique is designed to plug into contrastive models across vision, language, and graphs.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report consistent performance improvements across datasets from three modalities, including significant improvements for SimCLR on ImageNet-100, SimCSE on STS, and GraphCL and MVGRL on graph datasets.

narrative_sequence.summary: In-batch contrastive learning brings similar instances together and dissimilar instances apart within a mini-batch.
Existing hard-negative sampling is constrained by the instances available in the current mini-batch.
BatchSampler samples input-data mini-batches using a proximity graph and random walk with restart to select hard-to-distinguish instances while reducing false negatives.
The technique is presented as general across vision, language, and graphs, with reported improvements on representative contrastive models and datasets.
